![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217747/assets/ed702f9d982d599fc0f175dc7d7dd022aeefc3f5463aade2a9db71313faf4866.png)

Find the area bounded by the polar curve $r=1+\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \pi ,$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=1+\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\pi $, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}(\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{0}^{\pi })) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{|}_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{3}{4}(\pi -0)+(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0)+\frac{1}{8}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}+0+\frac{1}{8}(0) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
